definition: GLM, short for General Language Model, is a series of open weight large language models developed by Chinese software company Z.ai.
details: Though the first GLM model was published on 3 March 2021, it was released under the name ChatGLM as an AI-based chatbot in March 2023. It is also used in AI-assisted software development. GLM is the flagship model series of Z.ai, one of the six AI tigers of China. The weights of most GLM models are released under the MIT License or Apache License 2.0, allowing them to be run either locally or in the cloud.

explainer.lead: GLM, or General Language Model, is Z.ai's flagship series of open-weight large language models. Most releases use the MIT License or Apache License 2.0, so people can run the models on their own machines or in the cloud and build them into products such as chatbots and coding assistants.

tiers.eli5: GLM is like a very well-read helper that can turn a written request into a written answer, including help with computer code. Its maker, Z.ai, shares the instructions needed to run most versions, rather than keeping everything behind one website. That means people can use the helper online or set it up on their own computers.
tiers.practitioner: GLM models can be integrated into conversational applications such as ChatGLM or used for AI-assisted software development. Most model weights are available under the MIT License or Apache License 2.0 and can be deployed locally or in the cloud. Because the licensing statement covers most rather than all models, check the terms for the specific release you plan to use.
tiers.paperLevel: GLM denotes a series of open-weight large language models developed by Z.ai, formally General Language Model. At an application level, a selected model with weights theta maps an input sequence x to a generated output sequence y, written y = GLM_theta(x); available releases differ, and most weights use the MIT License or Apache License 2.0.

explainer.example: A developer could ask a GLM-based coding assistant, "Write a Python function that returns the even numbers from a list." The assistant would generate draft code for the developer to inspect and test before using it.

flow: A user or application supplies a written prompt to a deployed GLM model.
The model processes the prompt using its released weights.
It generates a response for a conversation, coding task, or another language-model application.
The application returns that response to the user or developer.
explainer.origin: The first GLM model was published on 3 March 2021. Z.ai later released it under the name ChatGLM as an AI-based chatbot in March 2023.
explainer.lineage: GLM grew from the model first published in 2021 into the ChatGLM chatbot released in 2023 and a broader model series. It is now the flagship series of Z.ai, one of China's six AI tigers.
explainer.whyItMatters: The series combines Z.ai's flagship language models with open-weight releases, giving users a choice between local and cloud operation. Its use in both chat and software development shows how one model family can support different applications.
